doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Metronomes, time and playing for dancers
summary: Metronome joke, Eddie Bert on swinging for dancers, and Gates's Lindy dance gigs.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: How do you teach people to do that?

I think metronomes are really important. Most singers hate them. Most musicians don’t like them because they’ve got this ugly click-click. But that’s — I tell them, I explain to them I say, “a long time ago metronomes were these big clumsy things that you’d wind up. Then they made them so you could plug them in the wall. Now they make them really small. So buy the smallest one you can, put fresh batteries in it, and swallow it. That way © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

you’ll always have good time.” Because time is what makes it happen. I mean I don’t want to hear somebody out of tune, but I’d rather hear them out of tune than out of time. Because if you’re in time at least there’s a groove. I mean I don’t want to hear out of tune either, but time, to me — I’ve been really fortunate in being around some musicians that I was buying their LPs when I was a kid. Eddie Bert said to me, “you know why we swing? Because we used to play for dancers. And we know how to swing. Because if they’re not dancing, we’re not swinging. And if they’re dancing and they’re swinging, they make the band swing even more.” So I also got lucky to play for dancers for a while. I used to play Lindy dances. I mean it was retro. It was like when people started to dance again, with dance societies. And I would get a call to play with the band, to sing a few numbers, because people were going to dance. And man the band would be swinging. So a lot of people don’t have the opportunity to play for dancers. That was a whole ‘nother thing. We don’t want to play for people to dance. We just want people to listen. I want people to want to dance. That means we’re swinging.
Yeah. Even if they can’t. Even if there’s no room they can feel it.

Yeah. They can groove at least. That’s what this music is supposed to be. It’s supposed to be a toe-tapper. Even if it’s slow. It’s supposed to make you feel some kind of pulse, some kind of momentum.
